knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Exhaust gas from a petrol engine, including carbon monoxide, can build up in an enclosed space. The machine must run outdoors and upwind of people and air intakes (general safety practice).
A warm power point and a loose plug are signs of a fault. The worker stops using the point and refers it to a licensed electrician. Taping the plug or using a longer lead does not address the fault.

Repairs are only for the manufacturer, its agent or a competent person, as the WorkSafe Victoria alert describes for equipment. The worker does not repair electrical faults on the equipment or the wiring.
Refuelling a running or hot engine is unsafe. The engine is stopped and allowed to cool before refuelling, and fuel is stored in an approved container away from ignition.
The lesson grants no electrical licence or authority to repair equipment or wiring. Repairing electrical wiring is licensed work in New South Wales (NSW-07, confirmed).

practicalCriteria: The learner inspects the power point, plug and lead, and records the result before connecting an electric machine.
The learner positions a petrol-engine machine outdoors, upwind of people and air intakes, with the exhaust directed away from the work area.
The learner stops the engine and allows it to cool before refuelling, and stores fuel in an approved container.
The learner stops and refers a suspected electrical fault without attempting a repair.
passRule: Knowledge checks: 80% correct (4 of 5). Practical sign-off is assessed separately by observation of the pre-use checks and machine placement. A knowledge pass does not verify electrical or engine safety in the field.
evidenceRequired: Pre-use inspection record for the power point, plug and lead
Equipment test or inspection record with the date
Record of machine position and exhaust direction for petrol-engine work
Fault and referral record for any defect
stopWorkCriteria: The learner runs a petrol-engine machine in an enclosed or poorly ventilated space.
The learner uses a damaged lead or a warm power point.
The learner attempts a repair to electrical equipment or wiring.
The learner refuels a running or hot engine.
